title: Linearizability and Amortized O(1) Guarantees for a TypeScript Ring Buffer Pipeline
topic: Ultra Low-Latency Ring Buffer Message Pipeline
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a lock-free ring buffer pipeline implemented in TypeScript that guarantees linearizability of message propagation while achieving amortized constant-time enqueue and dequeue operations. The design leverages atomic indices and a bounded circular array to avoid dynamic allocation and pointer indirection during runtime. Formal invariants are established over the buffer state, ensuring that each event is processed exactly once and in the order of arrival. Static analysis of the source yields a structural complexity of 199 SLOC and 11 function blocks, with a worst-case contention bound of $O(P)$ for P concurrent producers. Theoretical bounds are derived from the Michael--Scott queue model \cite{Michael_1996_SimpleFast} and adapted to the ring buffer context. No empirical wall-clock measurements are reported; all claims are supported by static AST inspection and formal proofs. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/typescript-design-patterns/tree/main/algorithms/20261011_084925_ultra_low_latency_ring_pipeline}
